reason: I'll strengthen the living bones first; the picture shows spaces for mineral and says it resists compression.
expectation: I expect the mineral to strengthen the bone framework, though I'm not sure exactly how it joins the fibres.

alternatives.reason: Building the front muscle also meets a goal, but I want to strengthen the framework first.

effect: The bones are strengthened while the elbow stays movable, so I can move on to building muscles.
reaction: The contrast between hard bone and the movable joint makes sense.
reason: I'll build the front muscle first; its tendon attachments show where the cells belong.
expectation: I expect muscle to form between the front attachments and help move the elbow, though I don't yet know how the game will show that movement.

alternatives.reason: The back muscle is also needed, but either side seems reasonable to build first.

effect: The front cells formed the biceps, which pulls to bend the elbow; the back attachment still needs a muscle.
reaction: Seeing how the pull bends the forearm makes the attachment's purpose clearer.
reason: I'll use the only available combination to build the muscle behind the elbow.
expectation: I expect a back muscle to form between the tendons and pull the forearm in the opposite direction.

effect: The triceps completes the opposing pair: the same kind of muscle cells can straighten rather than bend the elbow because of their attachments.
reaction: The matching pictures make the different pull directions clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the biceps and triceps was most worthwhile: their pull arrows connected attachment location to bending and straightening.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final muscle placement was less interesting as a decision because it was the only combination left, although its result completed the comparison.

surprise.text: I didn't expect the same kind of muscle cells to produce opposite movements just because of where they attach.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary: the bone window showed where mineral belonged, and the tendon spaces showed where to put muscle cells.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter to see more clear connections between body structures and their jobs, though the last choice here was predictable.
